To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) instantaneous values of leaf stomatal conductances as measured with a porometer need to take into account the temperature difference between the porometer head and the leaf surface; (2) this temperature difference may vary by more than 2.5 °c and may be larger than 10 °c; (3) this variation in temperature difference may cause large variations in the measured stomatal conductance; (4) this variation may also cause large errors in the upscaled values.

the temperature difference between porometer head (cup) and leaf surface is a crucial factor in the determination of stomatal conductance and that this temperature difference is often not properly measured.

the effect of the temperature difference between leaf and porometer head on the measurement of leaf conductance is large (up to 100% of uncorrected values) and that the accuracy of the correction is poor, in particular in the high conductance ranges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of stomatal conductance data obtained with dynamic porometers, which is a crucial issue for their use in ecological studies.
the accuracy and the reliability of the porometer measurements.
the accuracy and precision of stomatal conductance values as obtained with the Delta-T porometer and the effect of AT on the conductance values.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correction factor is very important and should be used in all measurements.
it is not possible, with current technology, to obtain accurate instantaneous conductance values with a dynamic porometers.

the use of uncorrected values of conductance should be avoided, and that, in the case of large temperature differences, a more sophisticated correction method than the one currently used by Delta-T is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is not possible to use a dynamic porometer to estimate stomatal conductance without correcting for temperature differences between the leaf surface and the porometer cup.
the temperature differences between the porometer head and the leaf are much higher than generally thought.
the temperature difference between the porometer head and the sampled leaf surface is a crucial parameter in the determination of leaf conductance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of a reliable method to measure the leaf temperature, a correction of the measured conductance values for AT is essential.

the temperature differences between the leaf surface and the porometer head are not negligible, especially when using a dynamic porometer with a small cup size and when measuring species with high stomatal conductance.
it is important to take the AT correction very seriously and that it may be better to measure AT directly, using a thermocouple.
